Every state where this registry lists a DataBank facility, Utah, Virginia, Texas, California, and Nevada, matches a market named on the company own site. The company page also references a partnership with Goodman Group to open a Los Angeles data center. No founding date, headquarters address, ownership structure, or acquisition history, and no building specific address or individual MW figures for this particular registry row, were located in available sourcing this session.

profile.campus_sqft_context: DataBank’s third data center on the Granite Point Campus, SLC4 leverages a private power substation to provide HPC-capable, high-density colocation cabinets ideal for compute-intensive workloads. The campus boasts outstanding connectivity with access to many carriers and cloud providers. 20,740 IT Square Feet

reading.body:
DataBank SLC4 in Bluffdale, Utah, publishes 3.67 MW of IT capacity, operated by DataBank.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 367 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 92 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

No compliance certifications are published for DataBank SLC4. That does not mean none exist, only that this site's dataset, built from the operator's own facility page, does not list any, which limits what regulated workloads a reader could confirm the facility is qualified to host.

Utah has 9 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 8 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 51.69 MW. DataBank SLC4 contributes 3.67 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
